subject: Urgent: CheckoutKit integration - intermittent high p99 and 5xxs after SDK v3.1.0
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@checkoutkit.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Team <sre@checkoutkit.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 latency and 502s after SDK v3.1.0

Hi Ben,

We started seeing an uptick in checkout failures shortly after we rolled your client SDK v3.1.0 on our frontend yesterday evening. Symptoms:
- p99 latency for /v1/generate requests jumped from ~250ms to ~2.4s
- overall 5xx rate rose from 0.4% to ~12% during peak (approx 18:30-20:15 PDT)
- observed a cluster of 502/504s, plus a handful of request timeouts on our side

I've attached a small trace sample (trace-20270920.log) and three request IDs: rQJ9-21, rQJ9-22, rQJ9-37. The commonalities in the logs look like partial header reads followed by parser resets, but it's noisy on our end. We also saw the frontend retrying and amplifying traffic which made throughput worse.

This is directly impacting checkout completion - conversion dropped ~4% in the window. Can you triage and let us know if this is an SDK issue or something we need to change server-side? We're keeping our rollout paused but need a clear plan and ETA.

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Head of Integrations, CheckoutKit

Attachments: trace-20270920.log (text/plain, 84KB)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High p99 latency and 502s after SDK v3.1.0

On Mon, Sep 20, 2027 at 10:35 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding CheckoutKit's escalation.

Quick triage findings from initial log analysis:
- The traces show repeated "incomplete header block" events in the SDK dechunker around the same time the client's frontend was under load.
- The Node.js http2 flow in v3.1.0 enables aggressive header coalescing to reduce syscalls; on lower-end customer frontends this can lead to split header frames being delivered in a way our streaming parser treats as a truncated header object, triggering a parser reset and request abort.
- When the client retries, the effective concurrency spikes and backend p99/layering worsens (retry amplification).

Short-term mitigations:
- Recommend CheckoutKit set SDK option sdk.http2_coalesce=false as a temporary client-side config to disable coalescing (we can provide a patch to expose this in their config quickly).
- Server-side we can add a tolerant header-merge window (small) to allow fragmented header frames to be reassembled before failing — will add as a hotfix (v3.1.1) and test under targeted load.

Action plan:
- I'll open INF-9876 and attach the trace snippets, plus a repro harness.
- If we can push v3.1.1 to NPM and publish a patch build within 8-12 hours we should see improvement; full rollout 24 hours after dry-run.

I'll follow up with a concrete changelog and a PR.
- Hannah (platform infra)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@checkoutkit.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@checkoutkit.com>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 latency and 502s after SDK v3.1.0

Hi Anjali — thank you for the traces and the heads-up. We're very sorry for the disruption.

What we've done so far:
- Our infra team confirmed patterns consistent with header/frame fragmentation in v3.1.0's streaming dechunker.
- We're preparing a patch (v3.1.1) that relaxes strict header assembly and adds a short reassembly window. Hannah has created INF-9876 (link below) and a repro harness.

Immediate asks for you (short-term):
1) If possible, enable sdk.http2_coalesce=false in your rollout to disable aggressive coalescing — we can provide a one-line change and a patch build.
2) If you prefer, we can route a fraction of your traffic to a fallback model variant while we validate the patch to avoid amplifying failures.

Timeline:
- Temporary client config guidance: within 30 minutes
- Patch (v3.1.1) candidate to you for validation: ~8-12 hours
- Target full rollout after validation: ~24 hours

We'll schedule a short exec sync later today so you have direct visibility. I'll include Sean and Marcus to coordinate credits/compensation and exec escalation.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec note: CheckoutKit incident and potential revenue impact

Quick executive summary for routing:
- Impact: CheckoutKit reported a +11% 5xx rate during peak window; p99 latency rose to 2.4s. Estimated revenue at risk ~ $45k for the window (customer-provided conversion numbers).
- Root cause hypothesis: SDK v3.1.0 streaming header coalescing + downstream parser strictness leading to aborts and retry amplification.
- Remediation: Hotfix v3.1.1 to relax header assembly, optional client toggle (sdk.http2_coalesce=false). Patch candidate today, rollout tomorrow after verification.

Please prepare a short exec-facing note (one slide + incident timeline). Also confirm whether we want to offer a goodwill credit or reserved-capacity rebate — finance/sales input needed.

- Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Engineering (internal)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Anjali Rao <anjali@checkoutkit.com>, SRE Team <sre@checkoutkit.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Patch v3.1.1 deployed to npm registry — validation and next steps

Hi all — quick update: we've published a patch candidate v3.1.1 to NPM and deployed a server-side tolerant header window to staging.

What we observed in the validation run:
- With sdk.http2_coalesce=false, the customer's repro harness shows p99 back near baseline (~280ms) and 5xxs drop to <1%.
- With the server-side tolerant window + v3.1.1 enabled in a small canary, the same improvements held under synthetic concurrency.

Next steps for CheckoutKit:
1) Apply the temporary client config (sdk.http2_coalesce=false) or pull v3.1.1 build for their frontend. We can provide the build and a one-line config immediately.
2) We recommend a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring on p99 and error-rate thresholds we will set up in Console.

Attachments: hotfix-changelog.txt, rd-incident-summary-20270922.pdf

Ben — happy to jump on a call with your execs and CheckoutKit if they'd like real-time validation.

Thanks,
Hannah
Platform Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
